reasoning_for_verdict: The new value asserts 1344 entries of a two-field record ({disposition, view_tag}) inside a *combat* golden leaf. Neither field name, nor the concept 'disposition', nor 'view_tag', nor 'S9' occurs anywhere in the 10.4 MB cached wiki corpus or in the formula document - so there is no source against which any entry of that map can be checked, let alone all 1344.

The formula document defines what a combat leaf is: a point estimate E[D | model, config], pinned by the golden snapshot; its Section 5 table enumerates every engine family that contributes combat output and all of them are numeric. A categorical label map with a presentation-layer 'view_tag' is not a combat quantity - 'view_tag' is a rendering concern, and rendering concerns have no game-verifiable value at all.

The count itself is unreproducible: no collection in data/ has 1200-1500 members, and 1344 is not any measured domain cardinality nor any product of one with a roster size. A 1344-entry payload also dwarfs the scenario it belongs to - the sourced content of 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is two items (Black Cleaver: 5 x 6% = 30% armor shred, 6 s; Bloodsong: 100% base AD spellblade + Expose Weakness 8%/5% amp, 4 s) applied across a five-man roster.

Project rule 5 ('no unsourced numeric literals; missing keys must raise') and the fail-closed posture of rules 6-7 both point the same way: an unsourceable 1344-entry blob does not belong in the numeric regression baseline. The prior state (<absent>) is consistent with every source in the evidence tree.
I cannot assert a *third* value (which is what 'both_wrong' would require), because the sources support no dispositions content at this path in any quantity. Absent is the sourced-supported state.
